title: Every Agent Artifact must contain a single Omni subtree with pre-declared emergency response protocols
content:
Although A.1.14.2.5.1 says "in general Omni Documents may have whatever content an Agent desires," it then imposes a mandatory skeleton on the free-form layer.

A.1.14.2.5.1.1 fixes the shape: "All Agent Artifacts must contain exactly one (1) Omni Document subtree. The head of this subtree is the Root Omni Document. All Omni Documents must be located in this subtree." A single rooted tree means every piece of non-primitive logic has one discoverable location — there is no second place to look, and nothing can hide outside the hierarchy.

A.1.14.2.5.1.2 requires a `Governance Information Unrelated To Root Edit Primitive` document as a direct child, defining "governance processes of the Agent unrelated to token holder voting." This is a deliberate residual category: whatever governance an Agent has that is *not* voting must still be written down in a known place.

Under it, two documents are compulsory and their split is the interesting part. A.1.14.2.5.1.2.1 requires a `Sky Ecosystem Emergency Response` document for "situations that impact the entire Sky Ecosystem," while A.1.14.2.5.1.2.2 requires an `Agent-Specific Emergency Response` document for "situations solely impacting the Agent, versus the broader Sky Ecosystem."

Forcing that distinction in advance is the substantive requirement. An Agent's duties diverge sharply between the two cases — in a systemic event it may have to act against its own short-term interest, and Sky Core may suspend its functions under A.1.14.1.5.4 — so the Atlas makes each Agent commit to both protocols while calm, rather than deciding mid-incident which kind of emergency it is having.
description: Exactly one Root Omni Document heads the subtree, which must carry a governance document whose children specify both an ecosystem-wide and an Agent-only emergency response protocol.
